reviews.text:
My Shih Tzu went in for grooming yesterday. Overall, she came out clean and her body and legs look beautiful, but unfortunately I did not get the cut I requested.

I had intentionally grown her face completely out and showed pictures of the round, full puppy-face style I wanted. Unfortunately, they removed a significant amount of hair from her muzzle, cheeks, and chin, leaving her face looking very narrow and skinny. The change is honestly jarring to me because it is the complete opposite of the full, round Shih Tzu face I specifically requested.

My Shih Tzu was brown with white patches as a puppy and faded to almost completely white as she got older. Sometimes people assume because of her coloring that she is mixed, but she is not. I know both of her parents personally. I specifically wanted a Shih Tzu-style puppy face, and unfortunately that is not what I received.

I also noticed that her ears were still dirty afterward. Maybe I should have specifically requested an ear cleaning, although I keep the hair out of her ears, so they are easy to access. She also did not have that fresh, good-smelling groomed-dog smell that I am normally used to after grooming.

Another downside was how long they kept her. I wasn’t expecting her grooming appointment to take several hours.

I paid $108 plus a $20 tip. I do want to be fair—the body cut is nice, her legs came out beautifully, and she looks clean and cute. I just really hate what was done to her face, especially after growing it out specifically for the style I requested.

If you’re looking for a general groom and don’t mind your dog being there for a while, you may be happy here. However, based on my experience, I personally would not recommend them if you’re looking for a very specific breed-style cut or particular facial shape.

On July 12th at 10AM, we dropped our two pups off to Spot Spot to get groomed. When my husband dropped them off, he requested them to be in two different cages (which is the smaller cages in the back). Around 3:50PM, the owner calls my husband and says that there was an emergency and he needs to come to the shop. When my husband asked if everything was okay, the owner then tells him that my oldest pup, Rhys, ran out of the shop 20 minutes ago. The owner said the cage wasn't locked properly and when another customer came in, Rhys ran out. After being  told by my husband to not to put him in that cage. I asked where he ran when he got out and they didn’t really have any information for me. They also have cameras that were conveniently not working. From 4pm to 4:45am, my husband & I walked around the area searching for our dog with other family member driving and friends walking. We had no luck after searching for almost 24 hours straight. We were not giving up. Rhys is everything to us and we needed him home.

Every time my husband went to the shop, the owner was always there as he claimed his workers were out searching for the dog as they still had other animals to maintain. When we went in the groomers there was another animal in the same cage that wasn't locking right / broken.

July 13th at 6AM, we went back out and were searching for our dog all over. We hung flyers out. The owner said he was hanging them all over however we only seen them in a few spots. We head back to the shop to ask more questions and ask for footage. And of course the camera weren't working or “not charged”. At 3:30PM the owner calls us and says that someone called him and they have our dog. He told us to meet him at the shop as he was already on his way in an uber to there. We never met the people who actually “found” our dog. When the dog arrived to the shop he was limping and had abrasions on his paws. He was also totally not acting himself even after seeing us. The owner stated he would cover our vet bills being as he is at fault and put my animal in danger because he did not listen to the correct safety protocols. We haven't heard from him since. Our vet bill was $620, we had to miss a day of work and send our kids to their grandmom house so they wouldn't know their pup was missing.

I’m extremely disappointed with my recent experience at this grooming salon. I brought my long-haired cat in for grooming, fully aware she had some knots in her fur. We explicitly told the staff it was fine to shave the knots but to otherwise keep her hair long. They assured us the process would take 3–4 hours, but after just one hour, they called to say she was ready. They explained that they had to cut her hair “a little shorter” to even things out and make the spots less noticeable.

When we picked her up, we were shocked to see that she was completely shaved down. This was far from what we requested. How does shaving her entirely count as “evening things out”? While they charged the amount they quoted, it’s frustrating to pay for grooming only to have her shaved—a task I could have done myself if that was the intended result.

This experience left me feeling that my instructions were disregarded. I trusted them to care for my pet and to deliver the service I asked for, but they fell short in a big way. Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this salon and will not be returning.
